# Conformance corpus

reStructuredText has no executable specification. Docutils is the oracle:
every expected output in this corpus is generated by docutils itself and
committed. Parser tests compare Alto Rst against these files, never against
hand-written expectations.

## Oracle version

- docutils 0.23 (also pinned in the `VERSION` file next to this README)
- Pygments is intentionally NOT installed: with Pygments present, docutils
  tokenizes `code` and `code-block` content and the output would depend on
  the Pygments version. The `directives/code-block` fixture relies on this.

`--verify` fails when the installed docutils version differs from `VERSION`.

## Layout

One directory per construct family. Each fixture is a pair:

- `<name>.rst`: minimal input, one behavior per fixture, `"\n"` line endings,
  ends with a newline, no dates and no absolute paths
- `<name>.pseudoxml`: verbatim docutils pseudo-XML output for that input,
  never edited by hand (it may contain characters the project style forbids;
  oracle output is kept byte for byte)

Families in v5 (111 fixtures):

| Family | Fixtures | Covers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| block-quotes | 4 | indentation quoting, attribution, nesting |
| bullet-lists | 5 | markers, marker change, nesting, multi-line items |
| comments | 4 | one-line, multi-line, empty, indented block |
| definition-lists | 3 | simple terms, classifiers, nested blocks |
| directives | 6 | note, image, code, code-block, option/body separation, unknown directive |
| enumerated-lists | 9 | arabic, auto continuation, start value, formats, mismatch recovery, loweralpha |
| citations | 4 | normalized labels, multiple definitions and references, multi-block bodies, unresolved references |
| footnotes | 7 | repeated references, mixed manual and automatic numbering, multi-block bodies, symbol order, mismatches |
| hyperlink-targets | 12 | internal, external, normalized names, anonymous ordering and mismatches, indirect chains and failures |
| inline | 14 | emphasis, strong, literals, references, standalone links, roles, substitutions, footnotes, citations, inline targets, escaping, quoting rule |
| literal-blocks | 6 | `::` forms, quoted literal recovery, indentation |
| paragraphs | 4 | single, multiple, line joining, backslash escapes |
| sections | 11 | underline styles, overline recovery, level order, short adornment, implicit targets and conflicts |
| substitutions | 8 | normalized names, nesting, replace, Unicode and image forms, introduced references, duplicates, undefined names, cycles |
| tables | 9 | simple and grid tables: heads, no heads, spans, multi-line cells, continuation, overflow |
| transitions | 4 | simple, at start, at end, too-short marker |

The ROM keeps substitution, footnote, and citation references as explicit
nodes while `ParseResult::references()` resolves them. Docutils writes the
post-transform tree instead, so direct ROM-to-pseudo-XML comparisons for
those families account for that representation difference. See
`_dev/knowledge/CONFORMANCE-NOTES.md`.

## Generation and verification

```
bin/conformance-corpus.php --generate   # refresh all .pseudoxml files
bin/conformance-corpus.php --verify     # regenerate to temp and diff, exit 1 on drift
```

The tool prefers `var/venv/bin/python` and falls back to a `python3` that can
import docutils. To create the pinned environment:

```
python3 -m venv var/venv
var/venv/bin/pip install docutils==0.23
```

The exact oracle invocation, for reproducibility:

```
python -m docutils --writer=pseudoxml --no-doc-title --no-doc-info < <name>.rst
```

- input on stdin, so `source` is always `<stdin>` (no absolute paths)
- `--no-doc-title --no-doc-info` disable the doctitle, docsubtitle, and
  docinfo promotion transforms: a lone top-level section would otherwise be
  rewritten into a document title and the section structure would be lost
- `DOCUTILSCONFIG` is cleared so user or system `docutils.conf` files cannot
  change the output

## Adding a fixture

1. Add `<family>/<name>.rst` (small input, one behavior).
2. Run `bin/conformance-corpus.php --generate`.
3. Review the new `.pseudoxml` by hand: the corpus is trusted because every
   expectation was read by a human once.
4. Run `bin/conformance-corpus.php --verify`.
